beats.text: A state machine diagram shows the states of one thing, and the events that move it between them.
Water can be liquid, vapor, or ice. Freezing moves it from liquid to ice. Condensation, from vapor to liquid.
Now an A T M. It starts Off. The black dot is the initial pseudostate.
Power on. It runs its startup and enters Self Test.
If the test fails: Out of Service. Otherwise, with no trigger at all, it moves to Idle.
A customer inserts a card. The A T M moves to Serving Customer, and on entry, it reads the card.
Serving Customer is a composite state. Inside are three substates in sequence: authentication, selecting a transaction, and the transaction.
The customer can cancel at any time. That goes straight back to Idle.
And whatever the reason for leaving, the exit action ejects the card.
A simple state has no substates. A composite state has substates. And a shallow history state returns to the last substate that was active.
